subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Instead of answering the question directly, the politician kept _______.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"beating around the bush"** means to avoid talking about what is important; to delay or avoid talking about something directly. (मूल बात को टालना)

 
 
• **Example:** Stop** beating around the bush **and tell me what you really think.
 
 
 
• Here the sentence is justified with the idiom 'beating around the bush.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Crying over spilt milk** (बीत चुकी बात पर पछताना): Complaining about a past event that cannot be changed.

 
 
• **Example:** There's no use **crying over spilt milk**; we need to focus on what we can do now.
 
 
 
• **Pointing at his laurels** (अपनी उपलब्धियों पर गर्व करना): Referring to one's past achievements.
 
 
• **Example:** Instead of addressing the current issues, he kept** pointing at his laurels.**
 
 
 
• **Spilling the beans** (राज़ खोल देना): Revealing secret information.
 
 
• **Example:** He accidentally** spilled the beans** about the surprise party.
 
 

38:Td8b,

The correct answer is **Option 2)**
